reference.title: Handstand Push-up
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching.

breathing.pattern: Breathe in at the top, hold a brace as you lower, breathe out as you press through the sticking point.
breathing.cadence: About 2.4 s down, short pause, about 1.4 s up

prescription.progression: Pike push-up, then feet-on-box pike push-up, then negatives against the wall, then full reps, then a deficit (hands on blocks)

cues.text: Kick up into a handstand with your back to the wall: hands just wider than the shoulders about a hand length from the wall, arms locked, heels resting on the wall.
Brace, bend the elbows and lower the head under control; the head travels slightly in front of the hands, elbows angled forward and out.
Crown of the head just above the mat: the head and hands form a triangle.
Breathe out and press the floor away, pushing the head back through the arms to straight elbows.
Lock out and stack the body; heels lightly on the wall.

mistakes.mistake: Crashing the head into the floor
mistakes.fix: Lower slowly, put a folded mat under the head and only go as deep as you can control.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flaring straight out to the sides
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows angled forward at about 45 degrees.
Brace the abs and squeeze the glutes; ribs down.

mistakes.mistake: Hands too far from the wall
mistakes.fix: About a hand length away; too far makes the body bow and the heels slide.

kinematics.norm: Hands just wider than the shoulders, about 10-25 cm from the wall, fingers spread (clinical opinion)
From locked out to about 90 degrees or more with the head just above the floor (clinical opinion)
Arms overhead (about 170-180 degrees) at the top (clinical opinion)
The head lowers slightly in front of the hands so head and hands form a triangle at the bottom (clinical opinion)
Body close to vertical, slight lean toward the wall, heels resting on it (clinical opinion)
Slow lowering of about 2-3 s; press as one smooth effort (clinical opinion)

sources.title: Marcolin, Petrone, Moro, Battaglia, Bianco and Paoli 2015, selective activation of shoulder, trunk and arm muscles: a comparative analysis of different push-up variants (J Athl Train 50(11):1126-1132)

cautions: Advanced: only attempt once you can hold a wall handstand for 30 s and do strict pike push-ups (clinical opinion).
Neck: never land on the head with force; use a folded mat or cushion and control the depth.
Avoid with uncontrolled high blood pressure, glaucoma, or recent head, neck or shoulder injury; being upside down raises pressure in the head (clinical opinion).
Wrist pain: the planted palm bends the wrist back about 80-90 degrees; use push-up handles or hex dumbbells to keep the wrists straight, or stop if pain persists (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Not yet strong enough: partial range to a stack of mats, or wall negatives only.
Wrist discomfort: parallettes or push-up handles.
